======================================================
 Md Tasleem @ Tasleem @ Tasleemuddin Son Of Md. Mujiburrahman @
 Mujubur Rahman @ Mojibur Rahman Resident Of Village - Dholbajja, P.S. -

 Versus  The State Of Bihar  ... ... Respondent  ======================================================
 Appearance :
 For the Appellant/s : Md Fazle Karim, Advocate  For the Respondent/s : Mr.Satya Narayan Prasad, APP  ======================================================
 CORAM: HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE SUDHIR SINGH  and  HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE CHANDRA PRAKASH  SINGH  ORAL ORDER  (Per: HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE SUDHIR SINGH)
3 19-05-2023
Heard learned counsel for the appellant and learned A.P.P. for the State.

The appellant has been convicted under Section 376 of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 4 and 6 of POCSO Act and has been sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a term of 20 years and a fine of Rs. 25,000/- under Section 376 of Indian Penal Code and in default of payment of fine, to further undergo additional rigorous imprisonment for a term of three months.

The appellant has further been sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a term of 10 years and a fine of Rs.
25,000/- under Section 6 of POCSO Act and in default of Patna High Court CR.
APP (DB) No.249 of 2023(3) dt.19-05-2023 payment of fine to further undergo additional rigorous imprisonment for a term of three months
. No separate sentence has been awarded under Section 4 of POCSO Act.
All the sentences have been directed to run concurrently.

It was further directed that the period of custody undergone by the appellant during the course of trial shall be set off under the provisions of Md Tasleem @ Tasleem @ Tasleemuddin vs The State Of Bihar on 19 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151603258/
1 Section 428 of the Cr.P.C.

sentences.text: By order dated 24.04.2023, the appeal was admitted.
The L.C.R. has been received.
It has been submitted on behalf of the appellant that the appellant is in custody since 19.12.2019 and has remained in custody for approximately three and a half years.
There is no chance of appeal being taken up in near future for hearing.

Learned counsel for the appellant further submits that as per prosecution case, it is alleged that on the pretext of marriage, physical relationship was established between the appellant and the victim.
Subsequently, the marriage could not take place for one reason or the other.
It is further submitted on behalf of the appellant that the said relationship was a consensual relationship between the parties.

In this regard, learned counsel for the appellant has placed reliance on cases of the Hon'ble Supreme Court since reported in 2019 SCC Online SC-3100 (Dr. Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.249 of 2023(3) dt.19-05-2023 Dhruvaram Murlidhar Sonar versus The State of Maharastra & Ors) and (2019) 9 SCC 608 (Pramod Suryabhan Pawar vs. The State of Maharashtra and Ors.).

sentences.text: After 22 days of the institution of the case, the victim gave birth to a child.
In the F.I.R. also, it is stated that due to physical relationship established between the victim and the appellant, the victim had become pregnant.

The D.N.A. test of the child (which the victim has given birth to with the appellant) was carried out by the F.S.L. Department in which it was found that the appellant is not the biological father of the child who was given birth by the victim.
This itself goes to show that the appellant had never established any physical relationship with the victim otherwise D.N.A. would have matched.
It is further submitted that no determination of age of the victim was made in terms of Section 34 sub section 2 of the POCSO Act.
He has further relied upon the case of JARNAIL SINGH Versus STATE OF HARYANA reported in (2013) 7 Supreme Court Cases 263.

entities.text: JARNAIL SINGH Versus STATE OF HARYANA reported in (2013) 7 Supreme Court Cases 263
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further pointed out that there is no compliance of Section 53A of the Cr.P.C.
In support of his contention, counsel for the appellant has relied upon the case of Chotkau Versus State of Uttar Pradesh reported in 2022 SCC OnLine 1313.

entities.text: Chotkau Versus State of Uttar Pradesh reported in 2022 SCC OnLine 1313
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Learned Additional P.P. appearing for the State has Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.249 of 2023(3) dt.19-05-2023 opposed the prayer for grant of bail to the appellant.
Considering the aforesaid fact, during the pendency of the present criminal appeal, let the sentence of the appellant aforesaid be suspended and the appellant be released on bail on furnishing bail bonds of Rs.10,000/- (Rupees Ten Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of Exclusive Special Judge (POCSO Act), Purnea in connection with Special Case No. 94 of 2019 arising out of Kasba P.S. case No. 248 of 2019.
The realization of fine imposed upon the appellant shall remain stayed.

(Sudhir Singh, J) ( Chandra Prakash Singh, J) Pankaj/-
